summary: ADR-0044 answers both questions and its counted facts check out against source: MemoryBinStore and LocalFsBinStore declare no presign (0), every SubscriptionTransport implementation in the tree is under src/test or src/clusterTest with M1.11b still `todo` (0), check-io-seam.sh line 58 filters exactly one module prefix, binstore-backends (1), and client/build.gradle.kts has api(project(":format")) and nothing else (1). Both check-module quotes are verbatim (NO_HTTP="format binstore-spi sequencer ingest" at line 234, the NOT-client-or-plugin comment at 228-230, NO_CLOUD="client plugin" at 236, the java.net.http comment at 260-262), and check-io-seam bans java.net/javax.net as packages (io_seam_scan.py:128-129) with the 11-file measurement at check-io-seam.sh:31-38. The arithmetic in (b) is right: putUvarint is LEB128 (SegmentWriter.java:46-53), 8,388,608 = 2^23 needs 4 bytes, 8 MiB/1600 = 5,243 bytes needs 2, the presence byte is real and written per grant (SubscriptionEvent.java:473-478), 1,600 x 7 = 11,200 and 11,200/8,388,608 = 0.1335%; 400 x 7 = 2,800 = 0.033%. It is an upper bound (a byteStart under 2 MiB encodes in 3 bytes, and a non-DIRECT event pays 0 rather than 1 because the flag lives inside the carriesGrant branch), so the decision does not flip. The doc 10 section 8 correction is fair -- the two degradation rows that touch the store really do say whole-object -- and the RunEntry/SegmentFormat/SegmentReader/SegmentWriter disposition is correct: those are the 48-byte directory entry's u64 byteStart | u32 byteLen (SegmentFormat.java:16-17), read on every decode at SegmentReader.java:87-98. Scope is clean: one backlog status cell, one new row, no production logic, no request-rate change. What blocks is criterion 3: the sweep table misses the two sites that still assert the dead justification in live prose -- research doc 04 section 2c's own revision banner, which the record cites in its Research header, and SubscriptionEventGrantTest -- and neither ADR says what became of security.md rule 3's range half, which ADR-0043 handed to this row by name while recording that it has no owner.

findings.title: the sweep misses doc 04 section 2c's revision banner, which still states all three claims ADR-0044 declares dead -- and a banner outranks the ADR by AGENTS.md's own rule
findings.failure_scenario: Criterion 3 names the patterns `byteStart`, `byteLen`, `M5.44` and `ADR-0043`; this banner matches all four and appears in no row of the sweep table, while ADR-0044's Research header cites this very section. It says (210-211) the fields came back 'because a reader given coordinates can issue ONE request where one without them reads the directory and then the payload'; (213-215) 'The single request spans `[0, max(byteStart+byteLen))` -- header included -- which R7's `h<headerLen>` makes computable in advance'; and (220-221) 'the coordinates let a node union its runs into one ranged GET without reading the directory, which is what "one grant per (node, segment)" needs'. ADR-0044 Decision (b) kills the first and third by name, and ADR-0043:74-77 already killed the second ('cost.md R7's h<headerLen> does not make that bound computable -- it gives the HEADER's extent, not the object's'), with the M5.45c cell calling that exact span 'UNREADABLE' because SegmentReader.open checks the footer magic first. Concrete failure: AGENTS.md states 'when an early conclusion and a revision banner disagree, the banner wins', and this banner is dated later than the prose it sits under. The next agent routed to doc 04 section 2c by the research skill -- M5.66's owner is the obvious one, since that row exists to decide whether a bounded read is worth building -- reads that `[0, max(byteStart+byteLen))` is computable from h<headerLen>, implements it, and every direct delivery throws 'segment is truncated: no footer magic' because the prefix has no footer. That is the same defect this row's own cell records round-1 review measuring inside ADR-0043: a correction applied to one of two places.

findings.title: the sweep table omits the test file that is about these two fields, and its live prose asserts the justification the ADR retires
findings.failure_scenario: The table has rows for GoldenSubscriptionEventTest and the six golden files but none for SubscriptionEventGrantTest, which matches `byteStart`, `byteLen`, `M5.44` and `ADR-0043`. Its class javadoc says the v3 event carries 'the range it is scoped to (M5.44)' and that ADR-0042 'named this row as the one deciding whether closing security.md rule 3's "where possible one range" means bringing them back. It does.' -- both now false: ADR-0043:112-121 keeps the grant scoped to the KEY and records that rule 3's range half is still open, and ADR-0044 establishes that no ranged GET is expressible. Line 265-267 is worse because the harness prints it: `.as("the range prints too, because it is not a secret and it is what a ranged GET was asked for")`. Concrete failure: the sweep's stated purpose is that 'corrected or confirmed' must be distinguishable from 'not looked at', and a reader who greps the two field names finds this file, finds no row for it in the record, and cannot tell which it was; then, when this assertion fails during M5.66's work, the message on screen tells the debugger the range is what a ranged GET was asked for -- the one sentence ADR-0044 exists to retract. The table's 'not this question' row is also short of its own grep: SegmentReaderTest.java, research docs 01/03/13 and ADR-0042 all match the patterns and appear nowhere, so the artifact does not support the claim that the sweep was exhaustive.

findings.title: security.md rule 3's range half was handed to this row by name and ADR-0044 never mentions it, while the ADR-0043 Status line added here declares the reopening closed
findings.failure_scenario: ADR-0043:112-121 states 'rule 3's range half has **no owner**' and that '"DECLINED" IS MORE THAN THIS RECORD KNOWS ... whether one ever becomes fillable is M5.45f's to settle'; its closing note at 215-218 repeats it. ADR-0044 contains no occurrence of 'security' or 'rule 3', and M5.66's new backlog row does not name it either -- it names the crossover measurement, the reader and the fields coming off the wire. Meanwhile the Status line this diff adds to ADR-0043 says 'The reopening under Decision (b) below is CLOSED by that record'. Concrete failure: at M5's milestone review the chain reads ADR-0043 -> M5.45f -> done, and rule 3's range half is marked settled having never been answered; or it is noticed and argued a fourth time, which is precisely what M5.66 was created to prevent. One sentence in ADR-0044 -- the range half is not closable until M5.66 makes a range fillable, and M5.66 carries it -- discharges it; without it the standard's clause is again owned by nobody, the failure this row's cell records review catching when the M5.45b split dropped it.

findings.title: 0.13% is measured against the segment, not against the stream the bytes are actually spent on, and the record then uses it as the price of keeping the fields
findings.failure_scenario: The arithmetic is correct and the denominator is named ('of the segment they describe'), but the 7 bytes travel on the subscription stream, which the same paragraph concedes ('it is *subscription stream* bytes rather than object-store requests'). A v3 DIRECT event encodes session, a 16-byte UUID, the segment key (~80 bytes for the key shape in SegmentKey's javadoc), the mode name and a presigned URL, so it is a few hundred bytes; against that the range is on the order of 2%, ~15x the figure the record prints. Concrete failure: M5.66's criterion 1 requires the crossover to be measured rather than asserted, and its owner reaches first for the number already written down; pricing the wire cost of the fields at 0.13% of the stream understates it by more than an order of magnitude. The decision does not flip either way -- the deciding argument is two format changes against zero -- so this is the label, not the conclusion.

findings.title: the new @param grant states a via/grant correspondence this record does not enforce
findings.failure_scenario: 'the signed URL under {@code direct}, {@code null} otherwise' reads as an invariant, and the compact constructor (lines 207-270) never inspects `via`: a caller can build INLINE with a grant, or DIRECT with none, and both encode and round-trip. The refusals that exist are grant-without-session-epoch, range-without-grant, half a range, a non-positive length and a negative start. This is the shape the same file already carries a scar about at lines 190-198 -- 'A LIVE SESSION NEVER USES THIS VALUE IS AN INVARIANT THIS CLASS DOES NOT PROVIDE, and an earlier version of this paragraph stated it flatly'. Concrete failure: M5.45g's criterion 2 requires a DIRECT delivery with no grant to be refused where it is BUILT; an author reading this javadoc concludes the refusal is already in the format type and puts none at the build site, and a DIRECT event with a null grant reaches a consumer that has nothing to fetch with.

verified: Counted facts (a), all four: `grep -rn presign --include=*.java` shows the only presign overrides in the tree are in ingest test fakes (StoreFakes.java:71,117,295) -- MemoryBinStore and LocalFsBinStore inherit BinStore's default-throwing one, so 0 production backends presign. Every `implements SubscriptionTransport` is under src/test or src/clusterTest (9 of them) plus the interface itself in client/src/main; M1.11b's backlog row is `todo`. check-io-seam.sh:58 excludes exactly `^binstore-backends/`, one module. client/build.gradle.kts declares one dependency, api(project(":format")).

Both gate quotes are verbatim and in the right places: check-module.sh:234 NO_HTTP="format binstore-spi sequencer ingest", :228-230 'NOT `client` or `plugin` -- the consumer must talk to the ingester, so an HTTP client there is the design, not a violation', :236 NO_CLOUD="client plugin", :260-262 'java.net.http needs no coordinate at all ... NO classpath check can see it'. check-io-seam.sh:31-38 carries the eleven-file measurement behind the named-not-derived exemption, and io_seam_scan.py:128-129 bans java.net and javax.net as packages, so (a3)'s claim that the import would be caught today holds (java.net.URI/URLEncoder/URLDecoder are the only prefix allowances, at :232-234).

The (b) arithmetic against source: SegmentWriter.putUvarint is 7-bits-per-byte LEB128 (:46-53), so 2^23 = 8,388,608 takes 4 bytes (the 2^21..2^28 band) and 5,243 takes 2 (the 2^7..2^14 band); SubscriptionEvent.encode:473-478 writes one presence byte then the two uvarints, exactly the 1+4+2 = 7 the record claims. 1,600 x 7 = 11,200; 11,200/8,388,608 = 0.1335% -> 0.13%. 400 x 7 = 2,800 -> 0.033% -> 0.03%. 1,600 runs per 8 MiB segment matches the corpus (doc 01 line 89, '48 B/run x 1,600 runs = 76.8 KiB on an 8 MiB segment'), and ~400 events per node matches ADR-0042:186-188. Both roundings are conservative for the decision taken.

The RunEntry/SegmentFormat/SegmentReader/SegmentWriter disposition is right and is not a dodge: SegmentFormat.java:16-17 puts u64 byteStart | u32 byteLen inside the directory entry, SegmentWriter:98-114 computes byteStart as PREAMBLE_BYTES + headerLen + running block length, SegmentReader:87-98 reads them per entry and bounds-checks against the footer start, and SegmentReader:138 slices DATA with entry.byteStart(). Editing those would change the segment layout. FetchPolicyConfig:19's 'coordinates' really is the send-a-reference sense.

The supporting format facts the record leans on are true: SegmentReader.open checks FOOTER_MAGIC at :68-72 before it walks the directory at :83-98, so a prefix throws 'segment is truncated: no footer magic'; codecFlags is per-run in the directory while DATA per run is [u32 uncompressedLen][u32 crc32c][records] with no codec id (SegmentFormat.java:14-21); SegmentKey's h<headerLen> is the header's extent (SegmentKey.java:17-23). Six subscription-event golden files exist, matching (b1)'s count.

doc 10 section 8's correction is defensible: of the four rows, the two that end in an object-store read say 'whole-object, no cleverness' and 'fetch by coordinates' (which SegmentReader serves from the directory), and the other two are a retry against another pod and a grant refresh, neither of which reads coordinates. The banner is placed under the paragraph it corrects and keeps the conclusion.

Alternatives: three under (a) and three under (b), each with a rejection reason; the two that decide the record carry numbers (11 files for a1, 0.13% and two-format-changes-against-zero for b1). Format matches the adr skill -- Status/Date/Requirements/Research/Context/Decision/Alternatives/Consequences -- and ADR-0043's body is left standing with the amendment on the Status line, which is what the skill's Staleness section requires.

Cost: no production logic changes, so no request rate moves. The record does not weaken M5.45g's criterion 6 (no production fetcher wired into a consumer path until M5.45h) -- it restates it as the only enforcement, and the backlog row still carries it. (b3) notes that a directory-then-slice read would be TWO requests where a whole-object GET is one, and M5.66's row carries that trade rather than assuming it; nothing here introduces a request that scales with records, shards, partitions or indices.

Scope: the backlog diff is exactly one status cell rewritten and one new row appended; M5.66's row is well-formed, cites NFR-4, states its dependency ('no dependency; it is a `format` question'), and its criterion 3 requires this ADR's Decision (b) and the new javadoc to be corrected when it lands, which closes the loop the field javadoc opens.

Criterion 2 holds: the amendment is on ADR-0043's Status line and not only in the backlog row. Criterion 3's chosen home is ADR-0044 rather than the ADR-0043 the cell names in bold; that reads as the better placement given the skill's no-body-rewrite rule, and the reason the criterion gives (diffable, inside the hash, not the commit body) is satisfied -- but ADR-0043's new Status line does not say where the sweep lives, so a reader following the criterion to ADR-0043 finds nothing.
